claims.text: The core language model used is AWD-LSTM.
claims.reason: Paper Section 3 states: 'we use the state-of-the-art language model AWD-LSTM (Merity et al., 2017a)'.

claims.text: General-domain pretraining was conducted using the Wikitext-103 dataset, which contains 103 million words from over 28,000 Wikipedia articles.
claims.reason: Paper Section 3.1 states Wikitext-103 consists of '28,595 preprocessed Wikipedia articles and 103 million words', which is over 28,000 articles.

claims.text: ULMFiT was evaluated on six text classification datasets.
claims.reason: Paper abstract and Section 4.1 confirm evaluation on 'six widely-studied datasets': IMDb, Yelp-bi, Yelp-full, TREC-6, AG, and DBpedia.

claims.text: IMDb is a binary sentiment analysis dataset.
claims.reason: Table 1 lists IMDb as Sentiment type with 2 classes and 25k training examples.

claims.text: Yelp has both binary and five-class versions used for evaluation.
claims.reason: Table 1 lists Yelp-bi (2 classes, 560k examples) and Yelp-full (5 classes, 650k examples) as separate datasets.

claims.text: TREC-6 is a six-class question classification dataset.
claims.reason: Table 1 lists TREC-6 as Question type with 6 classes; Section 4.1 describes it as 'six-class version of the small TREC dataset'.

claims.text: AG News is a four-class topic classification dataset.
claims.reason: Table 1 lists AG as Topic type with 4 classes and 120k training examples.

claims.text: DBpedia is a 14-class topic classification dataset.
claims.reason: Table 1 lists DBpedia as Topic type with 14 classes and 560k training examples.

claims.text: Slanted Triangular Learning Rates (STLR) linearly increases the learning rate quickly and then decays it slowly.
claims.reason: Section 3.2 describes STLR as using 'a short increase and a long decay period' with cut_frac=0.1, meaning 10% of iterations are for the increase phase.

claims.text: Gradual Unfreezing starts from the last layer (the least general) and moves backward through layers.
claims.reason: Section 3.3 states: 'gradually unfreeze the model starting from the last layer as this contains the least general knowledge', then unfreezing the next lower frozen layer each epoch.

claims.text: ULMFiT reduces errors by 18-24% in most cases compared to prior state-of-the-art.
claims.reason: Paper abstract explicitly states 'reducing the error by 18–24% on the majority of datasets', matching the summary claim exactly.

claims.text: With only 100 labeled examples, ULMFiT matches the performance of training from scratch with significantly more data.
claims.reason: Paper abstract states 'with only 100 labeled examples, it matches the performance of training from scratch on 100x more data'; Section 5 further details 10x–100x depending on supervised vs. semi-supervised setting.

claims.text: The authors used the Adam optimizer.
claims.reason: Section 4.1 states: 'We use Adam with β_1=0.7 instead of the default β_1=0.9 and β_2=0.99'.

claims.text: A specialized BPTT for Text Classification (BPT3C) is used to handle large documents.
claims.reason: Section 3.3 introduces BPT3C: 'In order to make fine-tuning a classifier for large documents feasible, we propose BPTT for Text Classification (BPT3C)'.

claims.text: Concat Pooling combines the last hidden state with max-pooled and mean-pooled representations to prevent information loss in long documents.
claims.reason: Section 3.3 defines concat pooling as h_c = [h_T, maxpool(H), meanpool(H)], explicitly motivated by preventing loss of signal in long documents where 'information may get lost if we only consider the last hidden state'.
